about: Col dei Venti (“hill of the winds”) is a small family winery in Castiglione Tinella, in the hills where the Langhe meets the Monferrato in southern Piedmont. Ornella Cordara, who grew up in a Piedmontese winemaking family, launched the label in 2005 with her son Ivan and her daughter Sara, who makes the wines. The estate is modest in size, about 10 to 12 hectares of vines and some 35,000 bottles a year, and it is listed in the Gambero Rosso guide.

The family farms a patchwork of parcels across varied hillsides with many microclimates, using organic and biodynamic methods and no chemical pesticides or fertilisers. Alongside Barbera, Cortese and Moscato from the home hills, they make Nebbiolo wines from the Langhe, including Barolo and Barbaresco under the name Tùfo Blu. Lampio is their Langhe Nebbiolo: the same grape as those grand wines, bottled under the broader Langhe appellation, which gives a more approachable, earlier-drinking expression of Nebbiolo. The 2018 has had time in bottle to soften: Expect plum and Maraschino cherry, a rich and elegant palate, hints of spice and sweet tannins.
